Brand name appears to be 'EmEL' on the machine body (photo 3, also faintly on photo 2).
Machine appears to be a straight-stitch style industrial head (no visible zigzag mechanism in the photos).
Photos show dust/wear and some scuffs on the base/stand (photos 1–3).
No clear view of model number/plate, motor specs, or control panel (photos 0–3).

risks.risk: Whether it is fully working (timing, feed, needle bar movement, and motor/drive condition). Photos do not show operation.
risks.proof: Video of the machine sewing a straight line on fabric (start-to-finish) plus a short clip showing the motor running and needle moving.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed working / needs service.

risks.risk: Exact machine type (some industrial heads look similar; could be different stitch class or missing parts).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the needle plate/feed dogs and the stitch adjustment area, and a photo of the model/serial plate.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic industrial straight-stitch head with unknown configuration.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/parts (presser feet, bobbins, needles, belt/drive parts, spool pin, foot pedal).
risks.proof: Photo list of included items laid out on the floor/table (presser feet, bobbins, needles, pedal, power cable, any belt/attachments).
risks.if_unproven: Price as machine only (no accessories included).

risks.risk: Condition of the stand/table and wiring (wear, loose connections, rust/corrosion).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the power cable, foot pedal connection, and underside wiring; also show the machine mounted securely on the stand.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming cosmetic wear and possible minor electrical/service needs.

proof_requests: Video: machine sewing a straight seam on fabric (with needle clearly visible) and showing the motor/foot pedal working.
Clear photo of the model/serial plate (or any label) on the machine head.
Close-ups of needle area + feed dogs + presser foot attachment.
Photos of what is included: foot pedal, power cable, bobbins, needles, presser feet, any belt/attachments.
response.reason: The photos identify an EmEL industrial sewing machine head, but the key pricing factors (confirmed straight-stitch type, working condition, and included parts) are not provable from the images alone.
